title: A son, Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī, is born to the Emperor's son Saʿd and Maryam, Shaykha of Qūnka: the first child of the line meant to rule the frontier
Joan, once king of Aragon and of Sicily, who lost Aragon to the Emperor Saʿd in the War of the Upper March, dies at sixty

The truce with Qashtāla runs out, and the Emperor Ismāʿīl declares the fourth war of the Istirdād, which he names the War of Jillīqiya. Portugal joins Qashtāla; Fās answers the Emperor's call with Tilimsān and Tafilalt. The Mamlūks, busy in the Fertile Crescent, are not needed

defenders.Castile: 1,650 regulars, 25 ships; 108 towns, 2,033,000 people, capital Valladolid, stability 6; King Pedro, 39, since 1394 (44/51/61, stubborn, a drunkard); heir Fernando, 18
defenders.Portugal: 750 regulars, 8 ships; 34 towns, 699,000 people, capital Porto; King Fernando, 45, since 29 April 1402 (37/41/59, deceitful); heir Joana

data.mamluks: called, but listed as potential; busy cleaning up the Fertile Crescent, and not needed (Trent)
data.levies: none raised on the day of the declaration
data.peace: nearly fifteen years since the Peace of Ramaḍān (22 June 1395)

title: The Catalan Merchant Privileges come back into force, sixty-four years after the war of the three crowns ended them. With Catalonia, Aragon and Valencia all ṭāʾifas of the crown, al-Andalus can no longer be at war with the Catalans, and the privileges can no longer be lost

data.effects: nobles power −20%, burghers power −10% (crown power +30% scaled by Farfanes in the army)

history.held: from the start of the game
history.lostAgain: by November 1346, in the war of the three crowns

data.why: the privileges need peace with Aragon; now that Catalonia and Aragon are subjects, war with them is impossible (Trent)

source: saves of 29 June 1410 and 1 November 1411; Trent's account

title: Off Cape Mondego the Castilian admiral Pedro, with 14 ships, falls on the fleet of Tilimsān, 13 sail, and sinks every one of them without loss
source: autosave of 1 March 1411 (the war's battle list)

title: At Peñafiel on the Duero the 970 men of the Ṭāʾifa of Qūnka attack the main Castilian host of 19,800 and are destroyed to the last man
source: autosave of 1 March 1411 (the war's battle list)

title: At Segovia the Aragonese, 1,035 under Ṭahmāsp, beat 500 Castilians led by the heir of Castile, Prince Fernando: 311 of theirs lost for 150
source: autosave of 1 March 1411 (the war's battle list)

title: At Cuéllar the Castilian host, 21,300 under Crisanto, attacks the Catalan army of 9,370 and breaks it: 5,400 Catalans lost for 2,000 Castilians
source: autosave of 1 March 1411 (the war's battle list)
